Edwin van der Sar has his wife to thank for promptly spotting the symptoms when he suffered a brain haemorrhage in 2023.

The former Ajax, Juventus, Fulham and Manchester United great has since gone on to make a full recovery, and appeared for an Ajax Legends side against their Barcelona counterparts at the Johan Cruyff Arena last weekend.

But at the time it happened, Van der Sar's wife, Annemarie van Kesteren, knew exactly what was happening having suffered a brain haemorrhage herself back in 2009.

Van der Sar told FourFourTwo: "Annemarie knew what was happening. I had this strange feeling that something wasn't right.

"Then before you know it, you see the light and the light hurts your eyes. I had pain in my head.

"From that point onwards, you just let yourself go, and hope the ambulance and the people around you take care of you.

"You have to put your faith, your life, into the hands of people who are trained for that and who specialise in it.".

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In a way, Van der Sar considers the timing to be fortuitous: he had only recent resigned as Ajax chief executive after seven years in the post.

He said: "I'd stepped away five or six weeks before [from Ajax], so I had all the time in the world to recover, rest and get better.

"If I'd still had the job, I think the eagerness and the demands of the position might have made my recovery harder.

"When you're responsible for a club, a manufacturer or an organisation, you want to be there.

"Luckily, I had no ties and nothing else to focus on apart from myself and my recovery. I've had a few chats - but nothing has really felt right.

"I'm enjoying my life at the moment, and I'm not actively looking for another position.".

Relive Starship's historic Flight 15 with our best photos from launch and 'Mechazilla' tower catch

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (880 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time.
  • In a recent development, flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov.
  • It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX has officially wrapped up the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket, successfully catching the vehicle's upper stage for the first time.

In a recent development, flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX's Starbase facility here in South Texas on Friday (Nov. 13). The mission was billed as the first to bring both of Starship's stages, the Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage, back to the launch site for recovery. And, while SpaceX was forced to divert Super Heavy's return to an off-shore splashdown (and explosion), the upper stage managed to survive its 22-hour jaunt in orbit and plunge through the atmosphere for a picture-perfect catch by the launch tower back at Starbase.

It was the first-ever Ship catch, and a huge milestone toward SpaceX's ultimate goal: making Starship completely reusable.

Recent findings suggest that liftoff occurred from Pad 2 at 5:47 p.m. EST (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local time) on Friday, against a near cloudless blue sky. Super Heavy is powered by 33 Raptor 3 engines, which provide more than 18 million pounds of thrust at liftoff. And lift off the booster did.

Starship roared off the pad under the power of those Raptors, pulsing visible shockwaves through the plume ejected from the rocket's flame trench.

The first couple minutes of flight went nominally; the vehicle climbed into the sky, gearing up for the hot-staging separation of Super Heavy and Ship — all of which was visible for miles, thanks to the clear Texas skies.

Space.com's images taken from the media’s launch viewing area were shot on a Canon R5 Mark II, with an RF 200-800mm lens that made the sharp pictures of Starship’s liftoff and return possible from almost 4 miles away.

This mirrorless Canon has specs that make it one of the best cameras available right now, with impressive features and functionality, including a 45MP sensor and excellent high-ISO handling.

Check our in-depth Canon R5 Mark II review.

According to recent reports, A successful separation occurred at T+2:21 minutes, as Starship soared approximately 40 miles (65 km) overhead. Once disconnected from its booster, Ship increased its thrust and continued onward to space, while Super Heavy, reoriented for its boostback burn and return to Starbase.

It has been revealed that that return, however, did not go entirely as planned. Super Heavy experienced a low-fuel alarm and autonomously shifted to an offshore splashdown rather than a catch attempt at Starbase.

Super heavy performed its landing burn above the Gulf of Mexico before cutting its engines for a brief moment and exploding in a giant fireball.

This was an intentional detonation, courtesy of the vehicle's flight termination system.

Sources indicate that ship continued on to low Earth orbit, where it deployed a payload of 26 upgraded Starlink Version 3 satellites. It was the second batch of V3 Starlinks delivered during Starship’s recent flight tests, each of which has added what SpaceX notes is the equivalent of 10 Falcon 9 Starlink V2 satellite rolls out worth of data capacity to its orbital constellation.

Flight 15 was also Starship's second-ever mission to orbit, and its longest so far. Ship spent nearly a full day in orbit, circling Earth a total of 14 times. During its jaunt in space, the spacecraft cleared three separate check points, which allowed SpaceX the opportunity to divert the vehicle for an ocean splashdown if needed, and finally was given the green light to attempt the first-ever Ship tower catch.

At approximately 4:18 p.m. EST (2018 GMT, 3:18 p.m. local time in Texas) on Saturday (Nov. 14), the spacecraft broke through the cloud cover that blanketed the skies above Starbase as onlookers watched its bellyflop plunge toward the ground. Moments after becoming visible, Ship ignited its engines for a flip and burn maneuver, which oriented it upright and swung its trajectory into the tightening grip of the chopstick arms of Starbase's "Mechazilla" launch tower.

After a slight sway back and forth suspended above Earth in Mechazilla's embrace, Ship came to a complete rest, hanging motionless as a historic milestone in SpaceX’s pursuit of fully reusable spaceflight.

Sources indicate that it hung there overnight as engineers, and even SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, inspected the spacecraft. Ship was lowered on Sunday (Nov. 15) and transported back to SpaceX's Starbase hanger bay for further checkouts.

SpaceX has not yet stated whether Ship 42 will fly again, but its return gives engineers a chance to examine how the spacecraft held up through launch, nearly a day in orbit and atmospheric reentry.

Those findings will help inform upcoming flights as SpaceX ramps up production to continue testing Starship's capabilities.

He has worked the space beat since 2016, covering the evolution of NASA's commercial spaceflight partnerships and crewed missions, planetary science missions, the Artemis program and humanity's return to the moon. He also enjoys building 1:144-scale model rockets and spacecraft. Find some of Josh's launch photography on Instagram, and follow him on X, where he mostly posts in haiku.

Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2065 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt.
  • In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus.
  • It has been revealed that back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty.

In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close.

It has been revealed that back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home.

Scared, exhausted and running on adrenaline, the team had lived through another episode of disruption; but in truth they had rarely known stability. For Syrian women’s footballers, navigating uncertainty had been part of the game long before the country’s political upheaval reached its latest turning point. “My generation was burned away and completely lost,” noted Noor Jumaa, a former national team goalkeeper. “It was like everything that was being built just disappeared.”.

Recent findings suggest that after 14 years of war, Syria has much to rebuild. Women’s football is among the institutions trying to recover from a conflict that erased an entire generation of players, interrupted the development of the game itself and left its infrastructure struggling. Yet, in recent years, Syria’s youth teams have emerged as one of the country’s more unexpected sporting success stories, winning regional titles and producing players who are beginning to make their mark abroad.

Syria’s women’s national team played their first international match in 2005. By 2011, prepares were under way for an 11-a-side women’s league. Then the uprising began, and all plans were abandoned. For the next six years, women’s football in Syria effectively stopped. There were no international fixtures at any level, only occasional futsal tournaments. More than six million people eventually fled Syria, including hundreds involved in the sport, leaving an already small pool of players scattered across the world.

Men’s football, by contrast, continued. The national team played matches abroad after Syria was barred from hosting fixtures in 2011 on security grounds. The Assad regime used its successes to project an image of normality, even welcoming the squad to his palace after their 2012 WAFF Championship victory. Fifa, despite its rules against political interference, stayed silent.

In a recent development, girls growing up in those years had no women’s team to watch. “I was watching a match of Syria’s men’s national team, and I was really upset. I would say, ‘God, if only they’d make a national team for girls,’” recalled Raneem Abo Lateef, a 21-year-old goalkeeper for Syria. The opportunity came unexpectedly after her family moved houses, and a girl next door told Abo Lateef that a relative was starting a girls’ club. “Girls’ football? Wow,” she said. “It was like dreams coming true.”.

Similarly, international teammate Julnar Mustafa spent hours playing with boys in her neighbourhood in Hasakah. Born in 2008, so too young to remember the beginning of the uprising, she filmed herself dribbling and performing tricks on her phone, uploading the videos to Facebook. A regional coach came across them and invited Mustafa to join his team.

Sources indicate that but finding an opportunity to play was only part of the challenge. “In our society, especially in the north, in Hasakah, sport is completely off-limits for girls,” Mustafa told the Guardian. “Not football, not anything”.

According to recent reports, while a new generation of girls were finding their way into football, the national team was attempting to return to international competition. In April 2017, Syria entered the Asian Cup qualifiers in Vietnam, assembling a squad after six years without any activity. The federation unveiled tryouts on Facebook, and players were given about a month of preparation. Syria went on to lose every match, including a 14-0 defeat by Myanmar. “Honestly, it was one of the worst teams in Syria’s history,” said Jumaa, who was part of that squad. “We lost by terrifying scores.”.

According to recent reports, maha Al-Katreb, also in the squad at the time, remembers the criticism that followed. Players were ridiculed despite having had little preparation. At the tournament, she saw opponents arrive with larger coaching staffs and younger players training alongside their senior teams. The gap between Syria and their regional competitors was difficult to ignore.

According to recent reports, with injuries ending her career early, Al-Katreb fell into coaching by chance and turned towards building a programme that could develop the next generation. She later joined the Syrian Football Association (SFA), taking on administrative and coaching responsibilities.

A six-team women’s senior league was established in 2019, followed by the development of youth national teams. This year the country held an inaugural edition of its youth league. Al-Katreb developed Syria’s first women’s football strategy, submitted to Fifa, that set out a longer-term plan for expanding participation and creating a pathway into the national teams. “You have to start building from the bottom if you want to see results after these 10 years,” Al-Katreb said. “So that we don’t burn one generation after another.”.

It has been revealed that in 2022, women accounted for only 1,000 of Syria’s 25,000 registered footballers. The women’s football strategy, seen by the Guardian, aimed to increase female participation by 150% over four years, including through 33 school training centres across 11 provinces, with capacity for 1,650 girls by 2026.

Sources indicate that the government has also outlined looks to rehabilitate the country’s sporting infrastructure. Rami Alsubea, an adviser at the Ministry of Sport and Youth, said in a statement that 48 sports facilities had been rehabilitated in 2025, with plans to rehabilitate about 150 more and build about 20 fresh ones by 2028. Restoring infrastructure is in part to meet hosting criteria set by Fifa and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).

Al-Katreb left the federation more than a year ago. Jumaa is now part of a two-woman team leading its women’s football department, appointed after the arrival of the federation’s current president, Feras al-Teet. Several players have criticized the federation’s leadership and the pace of progress. The Guardian reached out to Al-Teet for comment. He declined.

Among the players who have been vocal about the shortcomings is 26-year-old Rona Aizouk, one of the most experienced members of the current generation. Named after Brazilian footballer Ronaldinho, she made history in 2023 when she became the first Syrian-born woman to sign a professional contract, joining Saudi side Najmat Jeddah. Her performances in Syria had attracted the club’s attention, but securing the move proved difficult. Visa refusals and paperwork complications delayed her arrival until two days before the season began. Her time in Saudi Arabia lasted only a few months, and she was unable to extend her stay.

Recent findings suggest that “Honestly, I went there not wanting to come back,” noted Aizouk. “There’s no comparison. Everything is better, the treatment, the training, the facilities. It’s just different.

Sources indicate that “The most key thing is the players’ comfort. Here in Syria, we have to endure psychological pressure and torment. As a player, I have to fight the world just to achieve even a little bit of success.”.

It has been revealed that after returning to Damascus to complete her studies, Aizouk promptly received interest from multiple clubs in Jordan, where she now plays. For her, being in situ abroad is about more than personal progression. “I want to be a message that I, who came out of hard circumstances and out of a war, still managed to succeed.”.

Aizouk’s exposure to regional excellence has shown her that Syria is still many years behind. At the forefront is financial restriction that has left the sport bare-boned. International sanctions and banking restrictions imposed on Syria left millions of dollars in development funding from Fifa inaccessible to the SFA, preventing it from fully benefiting from programmes such as Fifa Forward.

Although broad economic sanctions have since been lifted, an estimated $11.5m in funds remains inaccessible to the federation. Both the SFA and Fifa insist they are working to establish a mechanism through which the money can be transferred. For now, the support has been seen in training equipment.

The financial strain is felt directly by players as both the national team and regional league are operated by the SFA. Clubs frequently go months without paying wages, and when payments do arrive, players say they can fall short of the amounts agreed. International call-ups offer little relief: during national team duty, including training camps, players receive a daily allowance of $20, capped at $200 for the length of their stay, regardless of how long it is. Some say the costs of travelling and playing can exceed what they receive.

Recent findings suggest that several clubs have folded since the domestic league’s launch in 2019, citing financial difficulties and the continued disruption caused by the war and ongoing conflicts. Those that remain often struggle to provide even basic resources.

Al-Hilal, now renamed Qamishlo Sport, have become one of the country’s most successful women’s sides, right now reigning as senior and youth league champions. But their achievements have not translated into financial security, according to head coach, Daleel Khalid. “There’s an absence of adequate support from all sides and the parties responsible for Syrian women’s sports, whether in terms of training camps and preparation, or the capabilities and infrastructure needed to develop the game,” he said.

The club’s campaign at the 2026 WAFF Women’s Clubs Championship was a big test. The tournament brought together league champions from six regional competitions. Despite having only a short training camp at home, Al-Hilal reached the final against Saudi champions Al-Nassr. Abo Lateef and Mustafa were among those who represented them, and their performances offered a reminder that Syrian teams can compete with the region’s best, even when their opponents have considerably greater resources.

According to recent reports, there was also individual recognition. Al-Hilal’s Mai Al-Jani was named the tournament’s best player after a series of standout performances, an achievement she was quick to share with those around her. “The award I won is a source of pride for me, for the club and for the players. I see it as a team award,” she noted. “It belongs to the staff, the players, and every Syrian girl living through these difficult circumstances.”.

Sources indicate that born in 2006 in a small village in Homs province, Al-Jani has emerged as one of Syria’s promising attacking talents. She won the league’s Golden Boot in the 2024-25 season and has continued to impress for both club and country. She was also named the best player at the 2023 WAFF under-17 championship, when Syria won their first international title in women’s football. Al-Katreb, who was an assistant coach, saw the victory as evidence of what the country could build with the right support.

The WAFF under-17 triumph was repeated at the 2026 edition with a completely different squad. “It was joy that everyone in the country needed,” said Jumaa. “We were completely outnumbered in technical and admin staff, with only nine of us managing everything. Other teams had double the number of staff, with gameplay technology we can’t get our hands on.”.

For Abo Lateef, the greatest risk is allowing another generation of players to lose the chance to compete. The senior women’s national team, for instance, has not played in over two years, with no reason given to players. “We need competition, regardless of the level,” said Abo Lateef. “I’m afraid a day will come when I’m made to sit at home, as was the case with the ones before us. A friendly fixture is a good start. Anything.”.

Aizouk’s message to those responsible for the future of the women’s game was more direct. “Save Syrian football,” she said. “Save the generations. Save us.”.

Mikel Arteta has confirmed he has taken “measures” that Arsenal players from selecting themselves or their team-mates on the Premier League’s Fantasy Premier League (FPL) game, in a bid to prevent his side’s line-ups and team news from being leaked.

It comes after eagle-eyed players of FPL, which has over 11 million total customers worldwide, spotted that Arsenal winger Christos Tzolis had selected himself to play against Liverpool earlier this month when he had been previously reported as an injury doubt.

Tzolis selecting himself in his line-up revealed that the winger was fit to start, however, and could have alerted Liverpool that he was ready to return to action and revealed notable team news before the match.

Chelsea’s Joao Pedro was previously revealed to be sidelined for their game against Tottenham after FPL players noticed that Chelsea staff had removed the club’s top scorer from their line-ups.

Arteta has now taken steps to ensure that his players cannot select anyone from Arsenal in their FPL teams, and even admitted that he is not sharing any team news with his children in case their teams were leaked.

"With Christos, with the squad, ‌with my kids as well, ‌they are constantly asking me about the line-ups as well because they want to know," Arteta said before his side travel to face Newcastle on Saturday.

According to recent reports, "The confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and what you're trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. And we will take measures to make sure that doesn't happen.”.

In a recent development, according to FPL tracking websites, Greek international winger Tzolis’s team is called ‘Tzatziki FC'. Screenshots of the teams line-up showed Tzolis had transferred out himself, Ezri Konsa and Riccardo Calafiori from his side before the Gunners beat Hull 1-0 last weekend.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If there’s one thing Brighton and Hove Albion know how to do, it’s sell players for sizeable fees and replace them with bargain signings who prove to be just as good, if not better.

Recent findings suggest that they replaced Yves Bissouma with Moises Caicedo, Robert Sanchez with Bart Verbruggen, Leandro Trossard with Kaoru Mitoma, and Marc Cucurella with Pervis Estupinan. Even when Caicedo and Alexis Mac Allister departed in the same summer, Brighton managed to maintain their upward trajectory thanks in part to the emergence of Carlos Baleba.

Now, having sold Baleba to Manchester United for £70 million, the Seagulls appear to have pulled off the same trick with another promising young midfielder: Chema Andres, who has developed a formidable partnership with veteran Pascal Gross in midfield.

Andres was still developing in Real Madrid’s academy less than two years ago. After honing his skills in the Spanish capital, he joined Stuttgart in 2025 for €3 million, where he rapidly established himself as an important figure in midfield, steering them to a DFB-Pokal final and Champions League qualification.

It has been revealed that he appeared destined to continue his development in Germany, but Brighton had other ideas. With just hours left in the summer transfer window, the Seagulls swooped in and signed him for £16 million. Fabian Hurzeler thrust him in at the deep end, and Andres swiftly repaid his trust by assisting on his debut at Coventry and leading Brighton to an EFL Cup victory at Old Trafford.

A midfield masterclass from @BHAFC's Chema Andres 👏 https://t.co/9s4FUF7Kd2October 3, 2026.

In a recent development, in just his second season of senior football, Andres is emerging as one of the Premier League’s top midfielders. Brighton sit second in the table, five points behind Arsenal, one ahead of Manchester City and 14 clear of relegation-threatened Manchester United. At the heart of their start is Andres, whose defensive discipline and penetrative passing has made him indispensable after Baleba's departure.

According to recent reports, while Baleba’s greatest strength lies in his ball-carrying ability, Andres offers Brighton a different route through opposition defenses. According to Gradient Sports, a football analysis tech giant, Andres is averaging 4.41 midfield line-breaking passes per 90 minutes, compared with Baleba’s 2.74 during his final season at Brighton. He is also completing 79.2% of these passes, well above Baleba’s 70.9%.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

That superiority extends to more audacious, high-risk passes: Andres is attempting 2.02 attacking line-breaking passes per 90, nearly twice Baleba’s 1.05, while completing them with far greater accuracy (90.9% vs. 71.4%). Whereas Baleba relied on his explosive acceleration to bypass opponents, Andres is using his vision, composure and passing range to slice through defensive lines and find his teammates.

Andres is also making his presence felt off the ball. While he might not be the same all-action midfielder who thrives on charging around the pitch and throwing himself into duels, his positional awareness and anticipation have proved invaluable in shielding Brighton’s backline. No Premier League midfielder has registered more tackles per 90 (3.31) or blocks per 90 (2.94) than Andres this season, while his 64.7% success rate in 50/50 duels exceeds Baleba’s 62.5%.

At 21 years-old, Andres is already imposing himself against the Premier League’s top sides. He excelled against Bruno Guimaraes and Declan Rice and found the back of the net in a 3–0 victory against defending champions Arsenal, before holding his own in a 1-0 win against Manchester City.

Despite costing Brighton less than a tenth of what City spent on Ayyoub Bouaddi, Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez combined, Andrés helped the Seagulls secure their first away victory against City in 18 attempts, before playing a pivotal role in their hard-fought 2–0 win against Brentford.

For all his virtues, it would be premature to declare Andrés an outright upgrade on Baleba. Nevertheless, his passing intelligence, defensive anticipation and tactical discipline could make him an even better fit for Hurzeler’s system. Rather than simply replacing Baleba’s qualities, Brighton have found a midfielder whose strengths complement their style of play, once again demonstrating their knack for staying one step ahead of the transfer market.

For a club that has built its reputation on unearthing hidden gems, molding them into stars, and selling them for astronomical profits, Andres is shaping up to be another transfer masterstroke. And if he can help Brighton secure a maiden Champions League qualification, Baleba’s departure might be remembered not as a setback, but as the catalyst for the greatest moment in the club’s history.

Industry observers note that after getting his big breakthrough as the co-founder of the football analytics website Breaking The Lines, Zachary Lowy has been able to tap into his footballing expertise for a number of esteemed outlets like ESPN, FotMob, The Times, The Independent and Urban Pitch. Since joining FourFourTwo as a freelancer in 2025, Lowy has been able to cover a wide range of topics from analyzing the sweeping changes to the MLS season to interviewing key figures like Asamoah Gyan and Rob Holding. Fluent in Spanish, Portuguese and Italian, Lowy’s versatile skillset has allowed him to traverse a number of different fields when covering major competitions like the FIFA Club World Cup. In addition to football, he is also a seasoned participant of other sports like pickleball, tennis, and volleyball.

Germany's 2027 budget: A record €561 billion and a mountain of debt

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1260 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • on Friday when the Bundestag's Budget Committee concluded its final session.
  • Following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget.
  • Sources indicate that reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was 5:55 a.m. on Friday when the Bundestag's Budget Committee concluded its final session.

Following nearly 16 hours of negotiations, lawmakers from the conservative Christian Democratic Union(CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties, along with their coalition partners from the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), voted in favor of the 2027 draft budget. The opposition parties — the environmentalist Greens, the socialist Left Party and the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) — voted against it. With that, the way is now clear for the final vote in the Bundestag on November 27.

Sources indicate that reading through the nearly 1,000-page document requires a great deal of number-crunching. Next year, the federal government prepares to spend around €561 billion ($620 billion).

But here's the problem: it won't collect nearly enough revenue to cover these expenses. With a shortfall of €123 billion, borrowing will be needed to bridge the gap.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But that's not the only problem. On top of all this debt, Germany also has loans for defense spending and for the renovation of the dilapidated infrastructure. Approved by the Bundestag in 2025, these special funds are set to be in place for multiple years.

It has been revealed that if the latest debt for 2027 is factored in, the total borrowing amounts to over €210 billion. This is the second-highest level of borrowing in the history of the Federal Republic of Germany. The only time Germany borrowed more was during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, when borrowing reached €215.4 billion.

Sources indicate that this development has drawn sharp criticism from opposition parties. Green Party lawmaker Sebastian Schäfer and his colleague Dietmar Bartsch of the Left Party called it a "gigantic mountain of debt," an "untrustworthy" budget, "irresponsible" policies at the expense of future generations and a lack of future prospects.

Industry observers note that to understand the reasons behind the growing debt, one has to look beyond the numbers. Every federal budget is a snapshot of the priorities set by a government and a country — in terms of the economy, social complications, security and geopolitics.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that for 2027, that story continues to be one of crises and wars. While Russia's war against Ukraine is driving up defense spending, the faltering economy is also demanding new investments. At the same time, Germany's population is aging rapidly, which is driving up social spending.

In a recent development, what's more, the crumbling infrastructure must be repaired and modernized, and the energy transition is costing billions. And more than half of all this debt is going toward security and defense.

Recent findings suggest that russia's war against Ukraine will enter its sixth year in 2027. As of the end of June, the federal government estimated its overall support for Ukraine to have reached approximately €100 billion. In response to a request from the AfD in the Bundestag, the government stated: "The federal government will continue to provide Ukraine with political, financial, humanitarian, civil and military support for as long as necessary.".

Industry observers note that the rearmament of the Bundeswehr and spending on NATO are also putting massive pressure on the budget. The defense budget is set to grow to just under €110 billion in 2027, an increase of around €27 billion compared to last year. Added to this are expenditures from the Bundeswehr's special fund.

Nevertheless, by far the largest single budget item comes from the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, which is set to grow to over €200 billion. There are prepares for cost-cutting measures, for example, in basic income support for job seekers. But the costs of old-age pension benefits continue to rise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

People born in the 1960s have begun to retire. Back then, more than 1 million children were born each year. But birth rates nearly halved in the early 1970s and have continued to decline since then. As a result, there will be an increasing number of retirees and a decreasing number of working-age individuals in the coming years.

The pension funds cannot be financed by the pension contributions of this dwindling workforce and have to be subsidized by the government. Already, contributions to the pension insurance system — which are split equally between employees and employers — will have to be increased. They are expected to rise to just under 20% of gross salary.

Industry observers note that the Federal Employment Agency, too, has long been unable to make ends meet on contributions alone. In 2027, subsidies of more than €8 billion from the federal budget are planned.

Anyone comparing Germany's current budget situation with that of past years will be rubbing their eyes in disbelief. It wasn't that long ago that Germany was considered a model of fiscal discipline. Between 2014 and 2019, the federal budget managed to avoid taking on upcoming debt for six consecutive years. In some years, there was even money left over.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, but the era of "balanced budgets" came to an abrupt end with the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. However, today Germany is still enjoying the benefits of those years of fiscal stability. Compared to other countries, Germany is still in relatively good shape.

The key indicator is not the amount of debt along but the debt-to-GDP ratio. It indicates how high the national debt is in relation to annual economic output.

At the end of 2025, it stood at 63.5% for Germany. France, on the other hand, stands at over 110% and Italy at about 135% to 140%, while the US is well above 100%. However, in its latest fall report, the German Council of Economic Experts warned that Germany could be heading down a dangerous path. If debt continues to rise at this rate, the debt-to-GDP ratio could climb to 100% by 2040.

This would also put Germany's creditworthiness on the financial markets at risk. Germany is the only country among the seven leading democratic industrialized nations (G7) that still holds a triple-A (AAA) rating. This is the highest possible credit rating on the financial markets. It signals to investors that the risk of default on German government bonds is extremely low.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

This also means that interest rates on new loans are not set as high. This is an important point, as interest payments place an increasing burden on the federal budget each year. By 2027, approximately €42 billion in interest payments are expected to be due.

At the end of November, the Bundestag will hold its final debate on the draft budget. Should changes be expected by then? There is disagreement within the government over whether a reduction in the electricity tax might still be possible.

The prospect of such a reduction had been raised by Chancellor Friedrich Merz. On Friday, during a European leaders summit in Dublin, he reiterated: "I expect that we will discuss this again next Tuesday in the coalition committee, and I remain committed to my goal of lowering the electricity tax to the European minimum — in full — starting next year.".

On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (654 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials.
  • They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico.
  • Industry observers note that it also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that on Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials.

They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster. The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA.

Industry observers note that it also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.

According to recent reports, the Arecibo message is only one of several messages intended for extraterrestrials, but this signal sent from Puerto Rico in 1974 was humanity's first intentional olive branch to the stars. At the time, it was the most powerful broadcast ever beamed into space, according to the SETI Institute.

Recent findings suggest that "The broadcast was particularly powerful because it used Arecibo's megawatt transmitter attached to its 305 meter antenna," SETI wrote of the broadcast in a project over. "The emission was equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast, and would be detectable by a SETI experiment just about anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna similar in size to Arecibo's.".

The message was designed by astronomy professor Frank Drake of Cornell University (who also developed the famed Drake Equation for alien life), as well as Cornnell graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan and others, according to Cornell University.

The message included 1,679 bits that were arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters per line, all prime numbers, with the broadcast lasting less than 3 minutes, according to SETI.

As of 2026, the message should have traveled about 52 light-years (1 light-year is the distance light travels in a year), with 24,948 light-years to go before reaching star cluster M13.

The Arecibo message may have been the first message of its kind, but it wasn't the last. We have also included messages on several spacecraft, such as Pioneer and Voyager. NASA and Paul McCartney also beamed a performance of "Across the Universe" in 2008.

Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia.

Hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She presently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jeff Stelling hosted Soccer Saturday for 29 years between 1994 and 2023 – but the end of his tenure has given him the opportunity to explore the world this year.

Stelling is presently starring in BBC One show Celebrity Race Across The World, having recently travelled from Borneo to Malaysia alongside his son Matt.

The rules of the expedition, however, meant Stelling wasn’t allowed to contact home or find out the scores of his beloved Hartlepool United.

Among the competition in the other three pairs were singers Sam Ryder and Ella Eyre, plus the offspring of Katie Price and Peter Andre, although Stelling admits to FourFourTwo that the show wasn’t exactly relaxed.

“It was incredibly stressful, because you’ve got no phone, you can’t find the football scores – no credit cards, £26 a day between the two of you for transport, food and accommodation, and you find yourself sleeping on floors, surrounded by rats in some cases,” he told us.

“But you see the most incredible sights, things I didn’t know existed. It was an amazing experience.”.

Even in the remote north of Australia, Stelling still heard the familiar catchphrase of 'Unbelievable, Jeff!' – once coined by his Soccer Saturday pal Chris Kamara.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

“Wherever I go, someone will shout it and laugh as if it’s the first time it’s ever been done…” Stelling smiles – in this week’s episode, it was clear that hearing the catchphrase cheered him up, after a tough few days of travelling.

“It became part of football terminology – could you believe from the beginnings of Soccer Saturday that, 30 years later, people still use it? When I was in Australia, a gang of guys outside a hostel shouted it.”.

Stelling travelled with his son on this occasion, having previously ventured to far-flung places with Kamara – heading to Sri Lanka on World’s Most Dangerous Roads.

If he’d had to choose a former footballer to travel with for Celebrity Race Across The World, who would have been the worst person he could have chosen?

Industry observers note that “Oh, Gabby Agbonlahor,” Stelling replies instantly with a laugh, referencing his talkSPORT colleague. “His geographical knowledge isn’t quite of the standard required. He couldn’t do Race Across Birmingham!”.

Stelling was speaking to FFT at the home of Woking FC as part of National League’s title sponsor Enterprise’s Local Legends campaign.

Nominations are being invited for unsung heroes across the league’s three divisions, with six eventually chosen to have their faces displayed on Wembley Way on National League play-off final weekend in May. Enterprise will also donate to community or charitable initiatives of all six associated clubs.

“In the National League, and National League North and South, virtually every club is the heartbeat of the community – there’s no other occasion when so many people from different walks of life within that community will be together,” says Stelling, whose boyhood club returned to the National League in 2023.

“Watching Hartlepool isn’t always therapeutic, but there’s nothing bigger in the community than Hartlepool United.

Industry observers note that “For clubs like us, when the good times are so few and far between, you remember them far better. When we won promotion from the National League to the Football League in 2021, it was one of the greatest days of my life.”.

There will be more from Stelling on his career in football in the next issue of FourFourTwo magazine.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Full-time defender and part-time model, the 31-year-old is happy to shine a light on both sides of his dual career.

“I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and mentioned: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi notes. He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds.

Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their upcoming manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons.

Industry observers note that “I’d get asked to go to a job or I’d even get booked for a job and they’d be like: ‘Oh, we want you to come to Germany for three days,’” Sowunmi says. “But I had to say: ‘I can’t do it, my priority is football.’ As fun and different as [modelling] is, it’s not my main job. Football was my priority and is my priority.

“It’s wicked, the stuff I’ve done modelling. Going to Milan fashion week, being taken to Paris fashion week with brands like Christian Louboutin is a level that I never thought I would reach or be possible when I first started it. Some of the people I’ve met doing it … when I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West … just celebrities and people that I grew up listening to and I feel like without that it probably wouldn’t have happened.”.

It has been revealed that sowunmi takes the Nobu Pilates with teacher Marsha Lindsay class twice a month in the five-star hotel of the same name in central London. He is an imposing presence at 1.98m (6ft 6in) tall and grimaces through the session as his muscles are put to the test to keep him in shape for both his professions. It helps him to battle robust strikers and appear on social media as part of modelling campaigns. “Two days ago one of my current coaches noted: ‘You popped up wearing a coat on my Instagram the other day. Can you get me one?’” Sowunmi says. “But I had to explain that it doesn’t really work like that.”.

Sowunmi’s career path since he left his first club, Ipswich, without making an appearance has been that of a true lower-league player, taking in spells at Yeovil, Colchester and – between two stints with Bromley – Sutton. On the catwalk, he has rubbed shoulders with some of the biggest names in the industry while promoting designer brands and plans to continue doing that once he retires from the day job. He uses social media not only to post videos and images from photoshoots but to show the reality of life as a footballer.

In a recent development, “The fans and everyone that watches you on Saturday or Tuesday or whatever day you’re playing, they get to see you for 90 minutes and they don’t see the full dedication that goes into being a professional footballer,” Sowunmi states. “We’re away from our families for two days [for away games]; we’ll train on the Friday then leave, maybe have a seven-hour coach journey. We’ll have stuff to do at the hotel, stretching sessions, pool sessions, nutrition. We’ll wake up and we’ll have more stuff to do and it’s that whole buildup that I kind of want to show them and give them an insight into what we do.”.

Industry observers note that last season Sowunmi helped Bromley gain promotion to third tier for the first time. The step up has been difficult, costing the long-serving manager Andy Woodman his job. “It’s been tough, as you can tell by the league position,” Sowunmi states. “It’s a completely different league. It’s taken a lot of the players by surprise, the difference between League One and League Two, but we’re grinding, we’re working hard and I’m sure it will turn for us.”.

A carefully curated moustache sits atop Sowunmi’s lip to raise money for Movember. He is speaking at a charity event on Wednesday to highlight the importance of mental health, a subject close to his heart since his best friend took his own life. “It’s something that is really deep in my heart just being a voice for people and trying to help make a difference in any way that I can,” Sowunmi claims. “I was actually on an away trip and I received a call from his dad to give me the news.

It has been revealed that “Everyone was asking me what was wrong on the bus and that I wasn’t really speaking to anyone and then I think when we got home it was a four-, five-hour journey. The manager took me to the side and got me to open up to him a little bit. Looking back that actually helped a lot, so I thought if I can help someone to speak to someone or know that it’s fine to speak to someone then I’m definitely here for it.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Craig McLeish worked his way up from St Mirren's youth coaching ranks to become first-team manager.
  • It is "damning" that Scottish FA chief football officer Craig Mulholland should have to "pander to clubs" as he attempts to bring in reforms, according to St Mirren manager Craig McLeish.
  • Mulholland and the SFA have engaged with Scottish Professional Football League clubs to encourage more playing time for younger players, but media speculation suggests those plans have been diluted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Craig McLeish worked his way up from St Mirren's youth coaching ranks to become first-team manager.

It is "damning" that Scottish FA chief football officer Craig Mulholland should have to "pander to clubs" as he attempts to bring in reforms, according to St Mirren manager Craig McLeish.

Mulholland and the SFA have engaged with Scottish Professional Football League clubs to encourage more playing time for younger players, but media speculation suggests those plans have been diluted.

And McLeish, who took over at St Mirren earlier this year, commented: "That's damning that he's having to change his looks to pander to clubs who aren't really on board with it and don't really have the best interests of the Scottish national team at heart.

"I understand why. We have owners from outwith this country. We have managers from outwith this country. They're in jobs, they're all fighting for their clubs.

"But why then are those people allowed to be the ones that hold the keys to the future of our country and the development of our national team?

"It's the way governance is set up and we've killed ourselves with that because the people who actually have a say in it have, not have no interest but they've got self-interest, and there's a lot of self-interest at the top end.

"I just don't see a way that we can really properly change unless something to do with governance changes and I just don't ever see that happening. It's really sad.".

'Not fit for purpose' - Craig Mulholland on youth pathway.

After reaching three of the past four major men's tournaments, Scotland struggled in their recent Nations League campaign, while Premiership clubs have missed out on the Champions League proper over the past two seasons.

The SFA had proposed including two under-21 players starting in cup competitions and the same age group playing a minimum of 6% of all available minutes across a season in league competition.

"We always focus at the top end, what our league size is, quotas for young players, a national base," 36-year-old McLeish, who worked in St Mirren's youth academy before his current role, said.

It has been revealed that "We have a fundamental problem that starts at our youngest age groups, at four and five years of age, about how we actually teach kids to play. And, until you fix that, you can't fix the top end of it.

"It's crazy some of the stuff that's going on, the formats, how we teach kids. There's just a massive lack of education and expertise at the very bottom of our pathway.

"In this country, football's everyone's sport and everyone gets access to it, but if you take your young kids along to swimming or gymnastics or whatever other sport, you're there with properly qualified coaches, teachers who have maybe done things at the top levels of that sport.

"We have nothing without the volunteers that work at the bottom end of the grassroots game, but they're not teaching kids how to play football properly, in my mind.

"And you're just hoping that they get put with a volunteer coach that can teach them something, that they get in with a really good group at the youngest ages.

"Because that development between the ages of three and eight, if you don't get that right, you're dead. You can't do anything after that point and we don't do it well enough. And you're just chasing yourself and we'll never catch up.".

Reporting McLeish's remarks, the Press Association said it had asked the SFA for comment.

They echo those of Dundee head coach Steven Pressley, who said on Thursday that Scotland would benefit from the creation of a national football centre and likened the current structure of the game to building on sand.

Pressley calls for national centre to enhance Scottish game.

One day it will have to end for Harry Kane, but for now, almost 12 years into his England life, there is still no matching the wisdom and influence he has accumulated over all those games and all those goals for his country.

This would have been a great night by any measure for a man collecting his record-breaking 126th England cap. There was a handshake from Peter Shilton, now deposed as king of caps, and a flourish by Kane of his recently acquired Ballon d’Or, once his four children had accompanied him on to the pitch. These are the nights of which dreams are made, and yet – given the defining feature of Kane’s career – there was one more thing to accomplish.

That was a goal from the man who has ploughed relentlessly past the two great England individual landmarks of caps and goals. His second-half penalty won the game and, although he is not infallible from the spot, he is as close to that status as England have ever had. Age has not yet run him down, he can still bend the game to his will, and when it comes to the pressure moments, his longevity seems to offer the upper hand.

According to recent reports, this was always going to be Kane’s night, with a great banner on the west side of the stadium paying tribute to the England captain. The Prince of Wales was in attendance for the occasion, too. Luka Modric presented his former Tottenham Hotspur team-mate with a keepsake from the Croatian football federation. Kane had to wait for the second half for the most valuable offering of all.

After the hour, the Danish referee Morten Krogh was advised by his VAR Bastian Dankert to take a second look at a corner tangle involving Jarell Quansah, and decided to award the second-half penalty from which Kane scored. It was certainly clumsy, but these grapples have been overlooked by referees in the past. The 27th successfully converted penalty of the Kane England era followed, and the man himself played the full game.

Shortly before kick-off, Croatia captain Luka Modric will present England captain Harry Kane with a special gift from the Croatian Football Federation (HNS), marking his Ballon d’Or win and his achievement in becoming England’s all-time record appearance holder with 126 caps.

Modric is not in the starting line-up but the 41-year-old has 206 caps for his country and will present Kane with a specially crafted replica of the first football ever brought to Croatia, which English industrialists introduced to the town of Zupanja in 1880. This event is regarded as the beginning of organised football on Croatian soil.

England’s 3-0 home victory over Czech Republic last month left them on nine points after four Nations League group games.

It came after a 2-0 win in the away contest, a 7-0 thumping of Croatia and a 3-2 defeat against world champions Spain.

A draw tonight will be enough for Thomas Tuchel’s side to book their place in the quarter-finals of the competition.

The eight teams to finish in the top two of the four League A groups will play in the knockout rounds that start in March 2027.

The two worst sides to finish bottom are automatically relegated, while the other bottom sides and third-placed sides are at risk of relegation via a play-off.

Jude and Jobe Bellingham could become the first brothers to start for England since Gary and Phil Neville took to the field together 19 years ago, with Jobe included in his first senior squad.

Jack and Bobby Charlton are the only other brothers to play together for England in the post-war period.

It has been revealed that “It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great. To be called up for England is a dream itself and I’ve been so proud to have the opportunity to represent England at every age group.

“I think I maybe underappreciated how big it was going to be, how big the reaction was going to be,” he told the BBC.

“I think the actual moment when Ronaldo mentioned my name, it’s strange, it’s almost like a movie.

“It was a really unique feeling because it is different to playing a game or scoring a goal, because it is so individual, it is nothing you can kind of do.

“Your mind is playing games with you the whole night, whether it is going to be you or not.

“So, when he actually stated my name, it was just a crazy emotion.”.

Manchester United CEO Omar Berrada has claimed that five summer signings have helped make the club’s squad “fundamentally better” despite the club sitting inside the relegation zone.

United have hired their fourth permanent manager under the current ownership model in less than three years since Ineos bough a minority stake from the Glazer family at the start of 2024.

Mauricio Pochettino has succeeded Michael Carrick, who followed Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim in failed tenures at Old Trafford, with his first game in charge on Sunday at Liverpool.

United spent almost £150m in the summer and despite disastrous form and outrage from many fans, Berrada insists the group of five signings under Carrick last summer helped bolster the squad.

It has been revealed that "You have to take it in the context of the last few years," Berrada told Sky Sports. "The summer of 2025, I think the recruitment team was widely praised with the four players that were signed. And they did very well. They helped the team achieve Champions League qualification. When we look at this summer, we went in knowing what we needed to do.

“Of course, there have been different dynamics at play. It's probably been the summer or the transfer window where there's been the highest inflation in transfer fees.

Sources indicate that "And we've mentioned publicly and we've said consistently in the last few years that we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players for the right value at the right time in terms of what the squad needs. And when we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we're receiving a lot of criticism for it, but we're actually happy with the players that we bought.

"We think that Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos, and Karl Darlow - and let's not forget that we've also welcomed back Marcus Rashford, who had a very good season on loan at Barcelona - these are five additions that we think have made the squad fundamentally better.

"It's true that we lost Casemiro, who is a top player and gave a lot to the club. We also lost Manuel Ugarte to, unfortunately, an ACL injury. So our focus was very much about straightening the midfield. When we started the transfer window, we really only had Kobbie Mainoo as our midfielder. So we wanted to reinforce that, and we did it.".

Satellites now outnumber the visible stars above most towns

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (702 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye.
  • Sources indicate that that's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that presently circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers).
  • Recent findings suggest that the results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than 700 satellites are crossing the sky over an average mid-latitude town at any moment of the night, outnumbering in many cases the stars visible to the naked eye.

Sources indicate that that's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that presently circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). Analyzing data from Oct. 12 and 18 this year, researchers found that with a completely unobstructed horizon, 710 satellites were crossing the sky in every single moment of the night above an average U.K. town.

Recent findings suggest that the results were published as a non-peer-reviewed study conducted by engineering firm Accu Components, and is based on satellite monitoring data from the U.S. Space Force available through the public website CelesTrak. Although the researchers specifically focused on the U.K., they say that such heavy satellite traffic flows above most of Europe, the U.S. and other mid-latitude regions, especially between 40 and 50 degrees north or south.

"Most Starlink satellites orbit at around 53 degrees to the equator, so the satellites bunch up over the mid-latitudes. These worldwide figures are approximate, based on a global grid over a single day," Accu Components spokesperson told Space.com in an email. "Skies near the equator are the quietest, with around 490 satellites.".

Industry observers note that not all of those satellites are visible to the naked eye, the researchers said in a statement. Because satellites unlike stars don't produce their own light, they must be illuminated by the sun, while the ground below has already sunk into darkness, to be visible. According to the study, an average of 105 satellites out of those 710 were catching light as they zoomed overhead, shining as bright as stars.

In a recent development, the spokesperson noted that the actual number of visible satellites varies drastically throughout the night. During the hours after dusk and before dawn, a much greater number of satellites can be seen, while in the middle of the night most no longer catch any light.

Industry observers note that "For a typical U.K. town, around 300 satellites are catching the sunlight in the first hour or so after dark," the spokesperson stated. "That falls to fewer than 20 around midnight, then climbs back to around 300 before dawn.".

It has been revealed that for comparison, as little as a few dozen stars are visible to the naked eye in the dead of the night above large, light-polluted megalopolis such as London or Latest York, according to OwnStarMap. In suburban areas and smaller towns, that number grows to a few hundred. To get to a few thousand visible stars, one must retreat into remote countryside or isolated mountain ranges.

Recent findings suggest that the number of satellites orbiting Earth has grown steeply in the past decade, especially since Elon Musk’s SpaceX began launching its internet-beaming Starlink constellation. Satellite companies plan to launch hundreds of thousands, possibly millions of satellites in the coming decades. If those visions come to pass, the number of passing satellites will vastly outgrow that of stars almost anywhere in the world. The trend especially concerns astronomers who fear the impacts on humankind’s ability to study the Universe.

Recent findings suggest that satellites crossing the view of ground-based telescopes leave streaks in astronomical images and increase the overall brightness of the sky through the light they reflect down towards Earth. Gradually, even the most powerful telescopes could lose their ability to see the distant stars and galaxies that hold the answers to key questions about the history of the universe.

The study found that throughout the night, an average U.K. town sees 12,891 different satellites passing overhead.

Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Frank replaces Frenchman Pierre Sage at Crystal Palace.

Thomas Frank is happy to be "back in the circus" after speaking at his first news conference as Crystal Palace manager.

The 53-year-old, who was appointed on a two-and-a-half-year deal on Monday, has been out of work since he was sacked by Tottenham in February, less than eight months after taking the job.

But, rather than dwell on that disappointment, Frank hopes to use it as a learning exeprience as he attempts to improve Palace's fortunes and lift them off the bottom of the Premier League table.

"If you don't learn from any of your jobs, I don't think you reflect, I don't think you improve, and I don't think you get better," said Frank.

According to recent reports, "Of course there's a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I've learned, definitely.".

The Dane said he could easily have extended his break from football, which he used to travel to Japan and Australia, as well as "visiting friends and family, eating too well [and] drinking too much wine" back in his homeland.

"I was very aware I didn't want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time," he added.

"I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it's good to be back in the circus, but it's also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.

"I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea.

"I'm a little bit surprised by this feeling I have in the body, how good it feels.".

How Frank can restore reputation and save Crystal Palace.

Frank's Palace reign begins with a trip to Coventry City on Saturday (15:00 GMT) and he notes he returns to the dugout unbruised despite the way his stint at Spurs ended.

It has been revealed that "I think we all have an ego," the former Brentford boss mentioned. "Some are better at controlling it than others. For me, it's not the critics, it's more what I can learn, what I can prove, how I can get better.

In a recent development, "There's a lot of clever people out there, but the interesting thing is they only know 10 per cent of the truth. That's a tenth of the truth at Brentford, there's a tenth of the truth at Tottenham, and that's just the way it is.

"If you can't handle that as a coach or a player, then you shouldn't be in this business, and I'm very happy to be back in the game.".

Arsenal are causing a “transfer frenzy” in South America, over a highly-rated wonderkid.

That's according to a new report that says that the Premier League champions are looking to improve their squad over the long term, as much as they are interested in adding players who can help the team fight on three fronts.

FourFourTwo understands that manager Mikel Arteta is keen to add dynamic difference makers in attack – but Arsenal could well surprise everyone by adding a 19-year-old who isn't well-known to Premier League fans.

During Arteta's early tenure as manager, the Gunners leant into the South American market, bringing in Pablo Mari from Flamengo as the Basque boss's first signing, six months after landing Gabriel Martinelli from the fourth tier of Brazilian football.

Since then, Arteta has built around the likes of Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Magalhaes, while bringing in Argentine assistant Gabriel Heinze.

The champions may be about to land their first Paraguayan, too, with Sport Witness relaying reports that teenage sensation Eduardo Delmas could be on his way to London.

According to information from Deporte Total, Arsenal are “seriously pursuing” Delmas, with Gunners scouts watching the attacker score in Paraguay's Superclasico and legendary forward Roque Santa Cruz providing his opinion on the starlet.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Delmas's club, Olimpia, meanwhile, are looking for a record sale for their talent, with the likes of Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain also scouting the talent.

Arteta may well be able to offer a pathway to the first team that the other two can't, however, with the likes of Max Dowman and Marli Salmon both making regular senior appearances for the Gunners after emerging recently from the famed Hale End academy.

During Arteta's time in charge, the likes of Bukayo Saka, Emile Smith Rowe and Eddie Nketiah have all played prominent roles, while Ethan Nwaneri, Folarin Balogun and Myles Lewis-Skelly have all been given Premier League debuts before the age of 21, to demonstrate Arsenal's commitment to developing youngsters.

The report suggests that “Olimpia will include numerous performance bonuses so that the operation could be worth even more than his current release clause,” though the initial fee will be a significant one, too.

Club president Rodrigo Nogues explained in September that he wanted Delmas to become Paraguayan football's biggest-ever sale, with an asking price set at over £10 million.

Arsenal travel to Newcastle United when Premier League action resumes this weekend.

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (721 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season?
  • Lionel Messi has closer organization at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers.
  • According to recent reports, casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight.

Lionel Messi has closer organization at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m.

According to recent reports, casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami revealed his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004.

According to recent reports, all of these earnings figures were revealed as part of the MLS Players’ Association’s twice-a-year data dump, with the latter installment dropping hours before the league’s postseason commenced. While these figures don’t include transfer fees and therefore don’t tell the whole picture of a team’s investment in its roster, it’s a useful bit of insight in regards to how each team is spending on player wages.

Figures are players’ guaranteed compensation inclusive of base salary and all guaranteed bonuses; does not include marketing and other bonuses.

Thirteen of MLS’s 30 clubs have a upcoming highest earner after a busy post-World Cup transfer window. Two – Anders Dreyer (San Diego, $3.6m) and Mateusz Bogusz (Houston, $2.5m) – rose to the top after the departure of a higher-paid teammate. Lozano overtook the injured Riqui Puig after arriving with the LA Galaxy on loan from San Diego. Lewandowski, Griezmann, and Embolo hold similar status, while Charlotte replaced Wilfried Zaha with Allan Saint-Maximin ($7.2m) earning nearly three times as much as the Crystal Palace great.

It has been revealed that other top-earners signed from beyond the league are Brais Méndez (Columbus, $5.2m), André Luiz (Kansas City, $3.3m), and Kai Wagner (Philadelphia, $1.6m). Two strikers who were traded within the league mid-season signed fresh terms that made them their new teams’ highest-paid players: Rafael Navarro (St. Louis, $4.95m) and Dejan Joveljic (Seattle, $3.7m).

The standout failure of the new big earners is Alexis Sánchez. The 37-year-old Chile legend came to North America this summer, joining CF Montréal and making 15 league appearances for the Quebecois club but failing to register a single goal or assist. His $2.97m guaranteed compensation makes up 24.6% of the team’s wage bill.

Griezmann’s arrival means that Messi no longer carries the largest share of any team’s wage bill, as Orlando has dedicated slightly more to the Frenchman (49.5%) than Miami has to the Argentinian (47.7%). Lewandowski narrowly trails by accounting for 47.3% of Chicago’s wage spending. Importantly, Messi’s contract includes add-ons; a portion of Apple TV subscriptions, merchandise sales through Adidas and Fanatics, and an optional ownership stake in Miami when he retires.

Other notable new wages include former Middlesbrough attacking midfielder Morgan Whittaker (Colorado, $2.0m), former Watford and Everton midfielder Abdoulaye Doucouré (Charlotte, $1.0m), former Manchester United left-back Tyrell Malacia (Cincinnati, $1.04m), former NYCFC playmaker Santi Rodríguez (Columbus, $3.9m), South Africa striker Lyle Foster (Houston, $1.8m), former Celtic striker Kyōgo Furuhashi (LA Galaxy, $1.1m), Tunisia winger Elias Saad (Nashville, $1.7m), former Leeds winger Jack Harrison (New England, $3.65m), Côte d’Ivoire winger Bénie Traoré (NYCFC, $2.5m), former Netherlands striker Vincent Janssen (Portland, $1.75m), Tunisia winger Elias Achouri (San Diego, $2.6m), Scotland goalkeeper Angus Gunn (San Jose, $1.6m), and Southampton loanee Damion Downs (St Louis, $1.6m).

While this exercise cannot confidently include every transfer fee paid, the timing of this year’s drop after the regular season’s end allows us to size up how teams spent on wages against the league table.

Does spending more equal success? There’s a degree of correlation there, but it’s not strong.

How valuable is it to get a point in MLS? In 2026’s wage economy, exactly $512,394.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Mauricio Pochettino has confirmed Bruno Fernandes will remain his captain at Manchester United as he bids to transform a club in crisis.

Fernandes has come under criticism this season, failing to replicate his from from a historic assist-making season last term.

Yet Pochettino is adamant Fernandes will be United’s “leader” as he bids to inspire a more physical approach to mirror his preferred pressing philosophy ahead of Sunday’s first game against Liverpool at Anfield.

Recent findings suggest that “All the players, we were chatting, it was amazing from day one, Bruno is our captain, an crucial player,” Pochettino confirmed. “But all the players need to think they are important, from the bottom to the top.

“I spent three hours, chatting in my office, with all the players, maybe I miss some injured players. In the next few days, we will talk in an individual way with all of them. It’s important to listen to what they need to say, understand the place they are. Not only on the field, off the field, what’s going on. Some conversations, some collective way, meetings, but focus is on Sunday.”.

While Pochettino added that his priority is to provoke a response after the downturn under Michael Carrick this season, rather than build a long-lasting culture that he insists could take many years to cultivate.

“We arrived with the idea to create something from scratch, our own ideas and philosophy, in the way we like to work, we find supportive people in the club, that make it easy, the adaptation, at the same time, we need to improve the players, to create the way to find a way to perform,” Pochettino noted.

“We are not focused on culture, it’s a massive work, you need to spend 10 years to focus on culture, it’s clear, a historic club.

"When we arrive, we found a group of players that we propose to do the football that we feel, being brave, be Man United, you know? It's about proposing the idea, they buy that idea, to be brave and try take that to the field. It's a debate that I don't like to go in, we cannot talk about things without context.

“On the data without context, it's easy to manipulate the data, I need to be honest, sometimes the data can show some things. We'll try improve the data and numbers in every single area of the field. We are here, not to denounce things, we're here to build things, perform and win games.
